security_audit.summary: All 50 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, URLs, arrows, and relative documentation links. No network request, shell execution, reconnaissance, or executable path traversal appears in SKILL.md. A separate medium-risk issue remains because the user-derived save topic is not explicitly sanitized before filename construction.

remediation.issue: The save filename includes an unspecified <topic> value.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize the topic to a safe slug and reject separators, dot segments, control characters, and absolute paths before writing.

content.user_title: Plan Newsletter Revenue and Sponsorship Pricing
content.value_statement: Newsletter operators need a clear revenue plan without invented benchmarks. This skill models subscriptions, sponsorships, and growth loops with labeled assumptions and disclosure checks.
actual_capabilities: Models monthly and annual paid-subscription revenue from audience size, conversion assumptions, and tier prices.
Builds sponsorship inventory and pricing with CPM, click-based, or flat-per-send rates.
Projects revenue at audience growth milestones using stated referral, recommendation, or boost assumptions.
Labels each input and result as Measured, User-provided, or Estimated.
Checks sponsorship disclosures, claim substantiation, and commercial-mail consent gaps.
Produces a handoff summary for ROI, quality audit, claims, or consent workflows.
limitations: It does not provide built-in industry benchmarks for conversion rates, CPM, or referral performance.
It does not calculate final ROI, revenue per send, list value, or payback.
It does not score overall email quality or resolve claim and consent issues.
Its projections depend on accurate audience, engagement, pricing, and conversion inputs.

use_cases.title: Price a Creator Newsletter
use_cases.description: Compare paid membership and sponsorship options using current audience size, engagement, cadence, and pricing assumptions.

use_cases.title: Build a Sponsor Rate Card
use_cases.description: Define placements, price bases, floor rates, and fill assumptions for a newsletter advertising program.

use_cases.title: Forecast Audience Revenue
use_cases.description: Connect referral or recommendation growth milestones to subscription and sponsorship revenue scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Revenue Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Model monetization for my newsletter. I have [active subscribers], [open rate], and [send cadence]. Compare paid subscriptions and sponsorships.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with core audience and engagement inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sponsorship Rate Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a rate card for [active subscribers] and [open rate]. Include primary, secondary, and classified placements with CPM and flat-rate options.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Monetization Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare paid-only, sponsor-only, and hybrid plans. Use my [tier prices], [conversion assumptions], [inventory], [fill rate], and [cadence]. Label every assumption.

prompt_templates.title: Project Growth and Compliance
prompt_templates.prompt: Project revenue at current, 25 percent growth, and 50 percent growth. Include referral assumptions, disclosure checks, claim risks, consent gaps, and handoff recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an advanced plan with governance checks.

output_examples.input: A 20,000-subscriber weekly newsletter has a 40 percent open rate. Model one primary sponsor slot at a user-provided 35 dollar CPM.
output_examples.output: Sellable impressions per send: 8,000, User-provided. Primary slot price: 280 dollars per send, Estimated from the supplied CPM. Disclosure: label the placement as an advertisement.

output_examples.input: A 45,000-subscriber list wants a hybrid plan with a 10 dollar monthly tier and sponsor inventory.
output: Paid tier: conversion rate needs a source before MRR can be projected.
Sponsorship: choose CPM or flat pricing, then provide inventory and fill assumptions.
Growth: define a referral share rate and referral conversion before projecting milestones.

best_practices: Provide active subscribers, engagement rates, send cadence, monetization goals, and known price points.
Separate measured values from user assumptions and estimates throughout the model.
Review sponsor disclosures, offer claims, and audience consent before selling inventory.
anti_patterns: Do not treat estimated conversion rates or CPM values as measured facts.
Do not include unsubscribed or unconsented contacts in the sellable audience.
Do not use this skill as the final source for ROI or email-quality scoring.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide active subscribers, open and click rates, send cadence, monetization goals, existing revenue, and any known prices or targets.

faq.question: Does the skill include industry benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. Missing conversion, CPM, or referral inputs remain marked as needing a source unless you supply a benchmark.

faq.question: Can it create a sponsorship rate card?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define placements, inventory, CPM, click-based, and flat rates using your audience and engagement data.

faq.question: Can it forecast paid-subscription revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. It calculates MRR and ARR from active subscribers, explicit conversion assumptions, and tier prices.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROI?
faq.answer: No. It prepares revenue inputs and sends ROI, revenue-per-send, list-value, and payback calculations to a dedicated workflow.

faq.question: How does it handle compliance?
faq.answer: It checks advertisement disclosure, claim substantiation, and commercial-mail consent gaps. It flags unresolved issues for specialized review.
